newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oseberg partners to spend NOK 1 bln upgrading Stur.
newsitem.headline: Oseberg partners to spend NOK 1 bln upgrading Stur.

text.p: The licencee group of the Oseberg oil development will invest one billion crowns to upgrade the Sture oil and gas terminal, north of Bergen on the west coast of Norway, operator Norsk Hydro ASA said on Thursday.
The upgrade will accommodate increasing gas production from the complex once a planned new gas platform is installed and tied back to Oseberg field centre.

Oil and wet gas will be separated from dry gas on the new platform. Dry gas will be exported directly from the platform, wet gas together with crude will be transported through the existing pipeline together to Sture for processing.
The upgrade will begin in the second half of 1997 and will last two years. It will include construction of on-land storgae facilities.
Oseberg produces around 500,000 barrels per day and reinjects gas to maintain pressure for crude production.
The development will begin gas output in the second half of 1999 and will supply two billion cubic metres of gas per year under contract to Germany's Verbundnetz Gas (VNG).
